classification.difficultyReason: Apply standard side, diagonal and angle properties of marked special quadrilaterals.

content.prompt: Using properties of special quadrilaterals, determine the value of these pronumerals.

spec.description: Upright kite with two distinct pairs of equal adjacent sides, three angle labels and two upper-side length labels.
spec.mathematics: Upper adjacent sides have double equality ticks; lower adjacent sides have single equality ticks. Left and right angles are equal. Interior angles sum to 360 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens and pronumerals are visible; numerical answers are excluded.

answer.worked:
The opposite angles between the unequal sides of a kite are equal, so $a=100$. The marked upper sides are equal, so $b=3$.

Using the angle sum of a quadrilateral:
$$\begin{align*}c+100+100+50&=360\\c+250&=360\\c&=110\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Slanted rhombus with all four sides marked equal, both pairs of opposite sides marked parallel, two dashed diagonals and an angle arc left of their intersection.
spec.mathematics: All four sides have single equality ticks. Left/right sides have single parallel arrows; top/bottom sides have double parallel arrows. The top side is 2 cm and right side is a cm. The angle b degrees is between the two leftward diagonal rays.
spec.answerVisibility: The diagonal angle remains labelled b degrees; no right-angle square or numerical answer is added.

answer.worked: All sides of a rhombus are equal, so $a=2$. The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular, so $b=90$.

spec.description: Tall slanted parallelogram with both diagonals dashed, diagonal-half length labels and angle labels at top-left and bottom-right.
spec.mathematics: The bottom-left to top-right diagonal is labelled 5 cm on its lower half and a cm on its upper half. The other diagonal forms 70 degrees with the top edge and b degrees with the bottom edge. Top/bottom sides have single equality ticks and single parallel arrows; left/right sides have double equality ticks and double parallel arrows.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels appear; equal-half and angle results are reserved for answers.

answer.worked: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so $a=5$. The top and bottom sides are parallel. Alternate angles formed by the other diagonal are equal, so $b=70$.
